correctness.rationale: Use affine barycentric coordinates λ_i summing to 1 for the uniform simplex. Every translate of tS corresponds bijectively to constraints λ_i>=δ_i with sum δ_i=1−t. Intersection with S is another simplex with normalized volume (1−Σ max(δ_i,0))_+^d. If inside y with m=min λ_i(y), any translate missing y has some δ_i>λ_i(y)>=m and total positive offsets >=1−t, yielding missing-mass upper bound min{t,1−m}^d. Taking δ_i=m+ε, δ_j=1−t−m−ε, all others zero, approaches equality; for exterior y set δ_i=0>λ_i(y)<0 and concentrate 1−t on j, attaining min(t,1)^d. This establishes all-point all-scale depth, with maximizers every point for t<=d/(d+1) and unique centroid otherwise. The homothetic superlevel sets and depth survival distribution are barycentric simplex volume ratios; baseline atom 1−((d+1)t−d)^d for critical<t<1, vanishing at t>=1. Grünbaum’s known centroid halfspace bound gives positive explicit large-t difference. Independently checked 36 exact rational near-maximizing translations, including phase boundaries; no finite test is substituted for all-d analytic proof.
